item.title: Eastern North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
444
ABPZ20 KNHC 070512
TWOEP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
1100 PM PDT Sun Sep 6 2026

For the eastern and central North Pacific east of 180 longitude:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Hurricane
Lowell, located several hundred miles south-southwest of Lihue,
Hawaii, and on Tropical Storm Marie, located several hundred miles
west-southwest of Punta Eugenia, Mexico. The National Hurricane
Center has issued the last advisory on Post-Tropical Cyclone Karina,
located several hundred miles east-northeast of the Big Island of
Hawaii.

Offshore of Southwestern Mexico:
An area of disorganized showers and thunderstorms associated with a
trough of low pressure is located several hundred miles
south-southwest of southwestern Mexico. Gradual development of this
system is possible, and a tropical depression could form during the
middle or latter portions of the week while the system moves
generally west-northwestward at 10 to 15 mph.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...10 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...medium...50 percent.

$$
Forecaster Katz/Beven

item.title: Tropical Storm Marie Public Advisory Number 24
item.description:
Issued at 800 PM PDT Sun Sep 06 2026 
362 
WTPZ33 KNHC 070243
TCPEP3
 
BULLETIN
Tropical Storm Marie Advisory Number  24
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP132026
800 PM PDT Sun Sep 06 2026
 
...MARIE EXPECTED TO CONTINUE TO PRODUCE DANGEROUS BEACH CONDITIONS
ALONG THE COAST OF BAJA CALIFORNIA AND SOUTHERN CALIFORNIA
FOR ANOTHER COUPLE DAYS...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 800 PM PDT...0300 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...24.2N 123.2W
ABOUT 560 MI...900 KM WSW OF PUNTA EUGENIA MEXICO
ABOUT 695 MI...1115 KM SW OF SAN DIEGO CALIFORNIA
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...70 MPH...110 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...NW OR 315 DEGREES AT 6 MPH...9 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...983 MB...29.03 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 800 PM PDT (0300 UTC), the center of Tropical Storm Marie was 
located near latitude 24.2 North, longitude 123.2 West. Marie is 
moving toward the northwest near 6 mph (9 km/h). A slight turn 
toward the west-northwest is forecast later tonight. Marie is then 
expected to resume a northwestward heading at a faster forward speed 
by Tuesday.
 
Maximum sustained winds have decreased to near 70 mph (110 km/h) 
with higher gusts. Steady weakening is expected to continue for the
next several days, and Marie is forecast to become a post-tropical
remnant low Tuesday night or early Wednesday.
 
Tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 160 miles (260 km)
from the center.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 983 mb (29.03 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
SURF: Swells generated by Marie will continue to affect portions of 
the coast of the Baja California Peninsula and southern California 
for the next couple of days. These swells are likely to cause 
life-threatening surf and rip current conditions. Please consult 
products from your local weather office. A depiction of rip current 
risk for the United States can be found at: 
hurricanes.gov/graphics_ep3.shtml?ripCurrents
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 200 AM PDT.
 
$$
Forecaster Cangialosi

item.title: Tropical Storm Marie Forecast Discussion Number 24
item.description:
Issued at 800 PM PDT Sun Sep 06 2026 
178 
WTPZ43 KNHC 070243
TCDEP3
 
Tropical Storm Marie Discussion Number  24
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP132026
800 PM PDT Sun Sep 06 2026
 
Marie continues to gradually lose strength due to cool waters and
intrusions of dry air. The system still has a ragged eye feature,
but it has been losing definition over the past several hours. In
addition, deep convection around the center is decreasing in
intensity and coverage. The satellite intensity estimates have been
dropping and currently range from about 45 to 65 kt. Based on a
blend of that data and Marie's degraded appearance, the initial wind
speed is lowered to 60 kt, making Marie a tropical storm.
 
The storm is moving slowly northwestward. A general northwestward 
motion with some increase in forward speed is expected over the 
next few days as Marie moves into a weakness in the subtropical 
ridge toward a mid- to upper-level low. Little change was made to 
the previous track forecast, and this prediction lies on the 
northern side of the guidance envelope, in best agreement with HCCA 
and GDMI.

Additional steady weakening is expected as Marie moves over 
progressively cooler waters and into an even drier air mass over 
the next few days. In addition, southwesterly vertical wind shear 
is anticipated to notably increase beginning Tuesday. The 
combination of these factors should lead to Marie degenerating into 
a remnant low, which is now predicted to occur by 60 hours. The NHC 
intensity forecast is similiar to the previous one and generally in 
line with the bulk of the model guidance.

Even though Marie is well away from land, large swells from the 
storm have been affecting portions of the coast of the Baja 
California Peninsula and southern California. These conditions 
will likely continue to cause dangerous beach conditions over the 
next couple of days.
